newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Texaco to buy Kazakh Karachaganak gas stake - source.
newsitem.headline: Texaco to buy Kazakh Karachaganak gas stake - source.

text.p: Texaco Inc will acquire a stake in Kazakhstan's $10 billion Karachaganak gas project through British Gas Plc and Italy's Agip SpA, a senior source involved in the deal said on Wednesday.

"Texaco is going to come in, and they will do it by taking equal stakes from British Gas and Agip," said a senior Western source who asked not to be identified and did not disclose the size of the stake.
British Gas and Agip each hold a 42.5 percent stake in Karachaganak, one of the world's leading gas fields with recoverable reserves of 1.33 trillion cubic metres.
The source, speaking after an international oil and gas conference, declined to say when the deal would be finalised.
Russia's LUKoil confirmed that it would acquire a 15 percent stake in Karachaganak that was previously held by Russian gas monopoly Gazprom.
Viktor Demidov, LUKoil vice-president in charge of international development, said British Gas and Agip had agreed to LUKoil's acquisition.
Kazakh Oil and Gas Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev said Gazprom, which said in June that it would leave the Karachaganak project, had formally recommended that LUKoil take its place.
"And so two new partners will enter Karachaganak," he told the conference.
The Karachaganak field, in northwestern Kazakhstan, also has 644 million tonnes of gas condensate and 190 million tonnes of oil.
British Gas and Agip signed a two-year extendable deal in March 1995 for the field, which will be developed over 40 years on a production-sharing basis.
The project, for which a formal production-sharing contract must still be signed, is designed to reverse steep output declines at the field.
